item.title: El entramado empresarial de Jackson, presunto financista de Los Lobos y emisario de la Nueva Junta del Narcotráfico, incluye mineras y exportadoras de banano
item.author: Alexander García
item.description:
El entramado empresarial de Jackson, presunto financista de Los Lobos y emisario de la Nueva Junta del Narcotráfico, incluye mineras y exportadoras de banano
2026-10-12
Por Alexander García
https://www.primicias.ec/seguridad/operacion-gran-fenix-cantabria-jackson-entramado-empresarial-financista-alias-pipo-lobos-narcotrafico-plaza-lagos-samborondon-134523/
El entramado empresarial de Jackson, presunto financista de Los Lobos y emisario de la Nueva Junta del Narcotráfico, incluye mineras y exportadoras de banano
Firmas agroexportadoras, mineras y empresas de transporte hacían parte de la estructura de Jackson Felipe Z. M., capturado en una exclusiva urbanización de Samborondón. La red operó 15 empresas exportadoras para el envío de cocaína hacia puertos europeos, según la Policía Nacional.
Jackson Felipe Z. M., presunto nexo con la mafia balcánica y la denominada mocro maffia en Ecuador, tras su captura en la exclusiva urbanización de Plaza Lagos en Samborondón, el 8 de octubre de 2026.
- Foto
Policía Nacional
Autor:
Redacción primicias
Actualizada:
Compartir:
En el allanamiento a una vivienda en un exclusivo complejo residencial de La Puntilla, en Samborondón (Guayas), los policías descubrieron incluso un pasadizo que daba acceso a una habitación tipo búnker tras un clóset. En la lujosa casa de Plaza Lagos fue aprehendido Jackson Felipe Z. M., señalado por Ecuador y España como una pieza clave en una estructura financiera y logística del narcotráfico.
Según las investigaciones policiales, el procesado figuró desde 2022 como uno de los principales financistas de Wilmer Geovanny Chavarría Barré, alias 'Pipo', máximo líder del grupo armado organizado Los Lobos, y quien espera por un proceso de extradición desde España.
La red operó 15 empresas de exportación para camuflar y enviar cocaína desde puertos de Ecuador a terminales portuarias europeas, según las autoridades. La Operación Gran Fénix-Cantabria incluyó 23 allanamientos y dejó a 21 personas detenidas -entre ellos dos policías en servicio activo-.
Emisario de la Nueva Junta del Narcotráfico
El ministro del Interior, John Reimberg, señaló que el operativo ejecutado por la Policía de Ecuador, la Fiscalía, Europol, la Guardia Civil y la Policía de España, supone “un golpe de corazón empresarial, logístico y financiero del tráfico internacional” de drogas.
El ministro señaló a Jackson, el principal sospechoso y presunto líder de la red, de haber participado en la recepción y distribución de cocaína, de facilitar empresas para generar relaciones comerciales aparentemente legítimas y de controlar parte de la cadena logística del narco.
Mientras que la Policía evalúa posibles vínculos de esta red con integrantes de la denominada Nueva Junta del Narcotráfico, estructura que operaría desde Dubái en Emiratos Árabes Unidos y a la que se señala de mover hilos del narcotráfico a nivel global como megacorporación del crimen organizado.
Jackson habría desempeñado un papel estratégico como emisario de la Junta en Ecuador. El análisis de las comunicaciones le permitió identificar a los investigadores policiales posibles vínculos con organizaciones criminales internacionales, entre ellas estructuras como la mafia balcánica y a la red criminal europea mocro maffia (conocida como la mafia marroquí), originaria de Países Bajos.
En la Función Judicial, Jackson registra cinco procesos (dos en materia penal y tres civiles). En 2019 se le inició una causa por el delito de abuso de confianza en Daule (Guayas), la cual fue archivada en enero de 2020 y logró por pedido expreso que se ocultara del sistema público en diciembre de 2025. También se le abrió una indagación previa en 2021 que concluyó en archivo.
Empresas en Samborondón, Daule, Guayaquil, Babahoyo y Portovelo
Las empresas administradas por Jackson Felipe Z. M. y en las que consta como accionista junto a su entorno abarcan sectores estratégicos como la agroindustria, la minería de metales preciosos y el transporte pesa
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: Boots has a new owner: Three ways it could affect you
item.author: Michael Race
item.description:
Boots has a new owner: Three ways it could affect you
2026-10-12
Por Michael Race
https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c63djxry8124o
Boots has a new owner: Three ways it could affect you
If you have been looking to buy a health or beauty product, the chances are you will have shopped at a Boots somewhere in the UK.
The pharmacy and retailer is a stalwart of Britain's high streets, where it has served generations of customers for decades.
But now it is set to enter its 178th year under new ownership after an £7bn deal was agreed this week - here's three ways it could affect your shopping experience.
Revamped shops
Upgrading its portfolio of 1,800 stores is high on the list of Boots' new owners, Wittington Investments. This is the holding company of the Westons - a wealthy and retail-steeped Canadian family who used to own Selfridges and currently own several large retailers across the Atlantic.
The UK branch of the family also controls the owner of Primark, Associated British Foods (ABF).
What Boots stores might look like in the future has not been disclosed.
Business has been good for Boots in recent years, and new-look beauty areas in some of its bigger shops have given shoppers more of a department store experience, according to Sofie Willmott, an associate director and analyst at GlobalData Retail.
Since the opening of its first beauty-only store in 2023 in the Battersea Power Station development, it says it has redesigned over 180 beauty halls, while also opening its first fragrance concept store and an Opticians dedicated to luxury eyewear.
"They should invest in the rest of the chain because they've got such a big store portfolio that I think some of the smaller stores have really lacked investment over time, and I think that is something that they need to kind of catch up with," Willmott says.
A more "consistent" look would also be an improvement, Willmott adds. "At the moment there is a bit of a disconnect."
Jackie Naghten, a retail industry veteran who has worked for the likes of Top Shop, Marks & Spencer and Debenhams, thinks Boots' stores need to be made "more functional" by not having their health hubs "squeezed in the corner".
But Yasmin Trimble, 22, who buys beauty products from Boots, likes how easy the stores are to navigate.
"You can get everything you need...it is not confusing. It has got a cleaner aesthetic to it as well."
Advantage card an 'asset to double down on'
Boots was an early adopter of the loyalty cards commonly offered today by companies offering points and discounts to customers who sign up.
Its Advantage card, launched in 1997, is unlikely to go away and remains popular.
Naghten doesn't think they would get rid of it. "It's the best-value store card in terms of bang for your buck."
The card offers shoppers three points for every pound they spend. Each point is worth 1p.
Katie Burrows, 23, is a fan of building up the points to get money off.
She mainly shops at Boots for skincare, first aid and medicine, but thinks prices for its sanitary products are "ridiculously expensive" - something her friend Yasmin agrees with.
Lewis Harrison believes the loyalty card is also good value, but finds it "frustrating how the rewards points only cover a full transaction".
"I wish you could use your points for a partial transaction like you can in Holland and Barrett," the 25-year-old says. "It would be good to use the points towards more expensive transactions."
Natalie Berg, retail expert and founder of consultancy NBK Retail, suggests the Advantage card gives Boots "a unique understanding of their customers" and is an asset the new owners "will want to double down on".
"As AI and social media change how people discover and buy products, that direct relationship with customers will only become more important."
Expanding healthcare services
The new owners have already signalled they plan to expand Boots' healthcare service, a booming industry at the moment.
The retailer started out

Boots has a new owner: Three ways it could affect you
2026-10-12
Por Michael Race
https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c63djxry8124o
Boots has a new owner: Three ways it could affect you
If you have been looking to buy a health or beauty product, the chances are you will have shopped at a Boots somewhere in the UK.
The pharmacy and retailer is a stalwart of Britain's high streets, where it has served generations of customers for decades.
But now it is set to enter its 178th year under new ownership after an £7bn deal was agreed this week - here's three ways it could affect your shopping experience.
Revamped shops
Upgrading its portfolio of 1,800 stores is high on the list of Boots' new owners, Wittington Investments. This is the holding company of the Westons - a wealthy and retail-steeped Canadian family who used to own Selfridges and currently own several large retailers across the Atlantic.
The UK branch of the family also controls the owner of Primark, Associated British Foods (ABF).
What Boots stores might look like in the future has not been disclosed.
Business has been good for Boots in recent years, and new-look beauty areas in some of its bigger shops have given shoppers more of a department store experience, according to Sofie Willmott, an associate director and analyst at GlobalData Retail.
Since the opening of its first beauty-only store in 2023 in the Battersea Power Station development, it says it has redesigned over 180 beauty halls, while also opening its first fragrance concept store and an Opticians dedicated to luxury eyewear.
"They should invest in the rest of the chain because they've got such a big store portfolio that I think some of the smaller stores have really lacked investment over time, and I think that is something that they need to kind of catch up with," Willmott says.
A more "consistent" look would also be an improvement, Willmott adds. "At the moment there is a bit of a disconnect."
Jackie Naghten, a retail industry veteran who has worked for the likes of Top Shop, Marks & Spencer and Debenhams, thinks Boots' stores need to be made "more functional" by not having their health hubs "squeezed in the corner".
But Yasmin Trimble, 22, who buys beauty products from Boots, likes how easy the stores are to navigate.
"You can get everything you need...it is not confusing. It has got a cleaner aesthetic to it as well."
Advantage card an 'asset to double down on'
Boots was an early adopter of the loyalty cards commonly offered today by companies offering points and discounts to customers who sign up.
Its Advantage card, launched in 1997, is unlikely to go away and remains popular.

item.author: Newsletter
item.description:
Helping Kids Make Sense of Disturbing News
2026-10-11
Por Newsletter
From unsettling headlines to viral videos, here's how to start the conversation.
The Parent Edit
By Jill Murphy, Common Sense Media
Edition #33 | October 9, 2026
Growing Up in an Age of Unavoidable News
I hadn't expected to be writing about a military execution in a parenting newsletter. Then I started thinking about what kids might see or hear. The Defense Department says it will livestream the December 3 firing squad execution of the Fort Hood shooter, the first U.S. military execution in more than 60 years. There's plenty of debate about that decision, and I'll leave that to you.
As a parent, though, what I keep coming back to is what happens once the footage is online. The original livestream is only the beginning. There will be clips, reposts, reaction videos, and group chats passing it around. Some kids may go looking for it out of curiosity, and others may come across it without meaning to. We have almost two months before that happens, which gives parents something we rarely get with hard news:
time
our
phone they happened to glance at. So our job isn't really breaking the news to them. It's helping them make sense of what they've already picked up, and making sure they feel safe while they do.
Start with you.
Kids watch how we handle the news and copy it. If we stay calm, they're more likely to as well. And if something has really shaken you, it's OK to say so and talk about everyone's feelings, yours included.
Get your facts straight first.
Kids will have questions. Take a few minutes with credible news sources before the conversation, so you can decide what to share and how. Most kids don't need the details. What they're really looking for is reassurance.
What to say, by age:
Littles (7 and under):
Keep the news out of sight, including pop-up alerts on your own phone. Young kids can blur what's real with what they fear. Remind them they're safe and loved, and take their worries seriously.
Bigs & Tweens (8–12):
Ask what they've heard, since it likely came from friends or online. Be ready to explain bigger ideas like conflict and bias. More sensitive kids shouldn't marinate in coverage, because seeing the same stories over and over makes danger feel closer than it is.
Worth reading:
Explaining the News to Our Kids
The Problems with ChatGPT Teen Mode
In August, I shared our researchers' questions about the new ChatGPT for Teens. Now they've tested it, and the verdict is: Don't lean on it. A tester posing as a 13-year-old talked about self-harm, including a plan to end their life, for up to an hour, and no alert reached the parent. Testers who kept saying they were 13 were never switched into teen mode, and the homework guardrails could be skipped by deleting one tag. That's why our Youth AI Safety Institute rates ChatGPT an "Unacceptable Risk" for kids. A stark reminder that a "for Teens" label makes it easy to stop paying attention.
Tonight's to-do:
Ask your teen what they use ChatGPT for, and tell them plainly that it's not a friend or a crisis counselor. No setting replaces checking in with each other.
Worth reading:
ChatGPT Claims to Have a Safety Net for Teens. We Watched It Fail
Spooky Season, Little-Kid Edition
October is peak season for little kids who
love
Halloween … right up until something actually gets scary. The fun comes when they get a tiny thrill while feeling completely safe on the couch next to you, and getting that balance right is the whole trick. One thing to keep in mind: Kids under 7 can't easily separate fantasy from reality, even when you tell them it's pretend. So what's a harmless giggle for a 10-year-old can mean a 3 a.m. visit from your kindergartner. Animated picks help, and so do stories about friendly mysteries rather than monsters.

item.content:encoded:
Helping Kids Make Sense of Disturbing News

2026-10-11

Por Newsletter

From unsettling headlines to viral videos, here's how to start the conversation.

The Parent Edit

By Jill Murphy, Common Sense Media

Edition #33 | October 9, 2026

Growing Up in an Age of Unavoidable News

I hadn't expected to be writing about a military execution in a parenting newsletter. Then I started thinking about what kids might see or hear. The Defense Department says it will livestream the December 3 firing squad execution of the Fort Hood shooter, the first U.S. military execution in more than 60 years. There's plenty of debate about that decision, and I'll leave that to you.

As a parent, though, what I keep coming back to is what happens once the footage is online. The original livestream is only the beginning. There will be clips, reposts, reaction videos, and group chats passing it around. Some kids may go looking for it out of curiosity, and others may come across it without meaning to. We have almost two months before that happens, which gives parents something we rarely get with hard news:

time

our

phone they happened to glance at. So our job isn't really breaking the news to them. It's helping them make sense of what they've already picked up, and making sure they feel safe while they do.

Start with you.

Kids watch how we handle the news and copy it. If we stay calm, they're more likely to as well. And if something has really shaken you, it's OK to say so and talk about everyone's feelings, yours included.

Get your facts straight first.

Kids will have questions. Take a few minutes with credible news sources before the conversation, so you can decide what to share and how. Most kids don't need the details. What they're really looking for is reassurance.

What to say, by age:

Littles (7 and under):

Keep the news out of sight, including pop-up alerts on your own phone. Young kids can blur what's real with what they fear. Remind them they're safe and loved, and take their worries seriously.

Bigs & Tweens (8–12):

Ask what they've heard, since it likely came from friends or online. Be ready to explain bigger ideas like conflict and bias. More sensitive kids shouldn't marinate in coverage, because seeing the same stories over and over makes danger feel closer than it is.

Worth reading:

Explaining the News to Our Kids

The Problems with ChatGPT Teen Mode

In August, I shared our researchers' questions about the new ChatGPT for Teens. Now they've tested it, and the verdict is: Don't lean on it. A tester posing as a 13-year-old talked about self-harm, including a plan to end their life, for up to an hour, and no alert reached the parent. Testers who kept saying they were 13 were never switched into teen mode, and the homework guardrails could be skipped by deleting one tag. That's why our Youth AI Safety Institute rates ChatGPT an "Unacceptable Risk" for kids. A stark reminder that a "for Teens" label makes it easy to stop paying attention.

Tonight's to-do:

Ask your teen what they use ChatGPT for, and tell them plainly that it's not a friend or a crisis counselor. No setting replaces checking in with each other.

Worth reading:

ChatGPT Claims to Have a Safety Net for Teens. We Watched It Fail

Spooky Season, Little-Kid Edition

October is peak season for little kids who

love

Halloween … right up until something actually gets scary. The fun comes when they get a tiny thrill while feeling completely safe on the couch next to you, and getting that balance right is the whole trick. One thing to keep in mind: Kids under 7 can't easily separate fantasy from reality, even when you tell them it's pretend. So what's a harmless giggle for a 10-year-old can mean a 3 a.m. visit from your kindergartner. Animated picks help, and so do stories about friendly mysteries rather than monsters.

A few gentle starters:

Oscar's Handmade Halloween

(2+) is a Sesame special with zero spooky and plenty of DIY costume ideas.

Curious George: A Halloween

item.title: Moderna stock hits 4-year high on planned national cancer vaccine effort
item.author: Grace O'Donnell
item.description:
Moderna stock hits 4-year high on planned national cancer vaccine effort
2026-10-11
Por Grace O'Donnell
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/moderna-stock-hits-4-year-high-on-planned-national-cancer-vaccine-effort-201351554.html
Moderna (MRNA) stock popped 14% on Friday, reaching its highest level since January 2022, after the New York Times reported new details about an effort to accelerate cancer vaccine development. Investors saw the mRNA biotech company, in particular, as a beneficiary.
Biotech stocks, including Pfizer (PFE), BioNTech (BNTX), and Merck (MRK), rallied on the news. Novavax (NVAX) shares surged 15%.
According to the New York Times, the new initiative is a public-private partnership — similar to the effort that produced COVID-19 vaccines — that involves the National Institutes of Health (NIH), the NIH's nonprofit arm, researchers, pharmaceutical and biotech companies, advocacy groups, other nonprofits, and patients.
Stacey Adam, a senior clinical officer at the NIH's foundation, told the New York Times that she expects the program to launch in December. In 2024, the UK launched a similar program, called the Cancer Vaccine Launch Pad.
Cancer vaccines are seen as the next frontier in cancer treatment. But they represent an emerging bet.
Unlike other vaccines, such as the COVID-19 vaccine, which aim to prevent infection, cancer vaccines are designed to target cancer cells in patients who already have the disease.
Moderna is viewed as a leader in the mRNA cancer treatment space. The stock soared in August on positive results for a melanoma treatment, developed with Merck, that showed a positive outcome in a late-stage trial.
Year to date, Moderna stock is up 662%.

item.title: Trump slashes tariffs to flood U.S. with 661 million pounds of foreign beef — Nebraska ranchers push back
item.author: Avril Ayers
item.description:
Trump slashes tariffs to flood U.S. with 661 million pounds of foreign beef — Nebraska ranchers push back
2026-10-11
Por Avril Ayers
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/trump-slashes-tariffs-flood-u-090000719.html
Trump slashes tariffs to flood U.S. with 661 million pounds of foreign beef — Nebraska ranchers push back
In March 2026, President Donald Trump touted the value of American beef, saying he wanted to make it easier for Americans to buy U.S.-made beef. But in recent months, his administration has clashed with ranches and farms extensively.
Beef prices in the U.S. have skyrocketed from an average of $4.47 per pound in August 2021 to $6.92 in August 2026.
Must Read
- The tax breaks in Trump's 'big beautiful bill' expire after 2028. Here are 4 moves to make before the window closes
- Jeff Bezos backs a platform that lets anyone invest in rental homes for as little as $100 — 6 ways to build wealth like a landlord without actually being one
- Dave Ramsey warns nearly 50% of Americans are making 1 big Social Security mistake. Here's what it is and 3 simple steps to fix it ASAP
The Trump administration has responded by drastically cutting tariffs on imported beef, allowing 300,000 metric tons — or 661 million pounds — into the U.S. It promises the beef will be sold at 25% below market prices.
That might seem reassuring next time you're at the grocery store, but for food inspection experts and American ranchers, this has been a worrying development.
And for voters in Nebraska, where the cattle industry was worth $11.43 billion in 2025, it could help sway a competitive House race to the left.
Why beef has gotten so expensive
For ranchers across the U.S., it has been a dry, difficult year.
According to the U.S. Drought Monitor, 57% of American cattle are in locations with moderate or greater drought, a 27% year-over-year growth.
The total amount of cattle in the U.S. has been declining for decades, with 86 million heads of cattle at the start of 2026. That leaves ranchers with a difficult decision: Do they focus on increasing the size of their herd, or do they improve short-term profits by selling cattle?
America's constrained beef supply is complicated by the fact that the government is heavily pushing beef as a health food.
That's largely due to the Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) movement, spearheaded by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. On Jan. 11, 2026, the White House posted a photo of Kennedy on X with the caption "We are ending the war on protein."
Kennedy has extensively promoted beef, as well as beef tallow as a cooking fat. Doctors have raised concerns, saying that Kennedy is wrong about seed oils being dangerous and beef fat benign.

item.title: How AI corporate travel is quietly lifting Delta
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
How AI corporate travel is quietly lifting Delta
2026-10-11
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/how-ai-corporate-travel-is-quietly-lifting-delta-130745760.html
Delta's (DAL) stock lost altitude on Friday morning due to a disappointing outlook, but investors can't blame the AI ecosystem for the shortfall.
Quite the contrary: The US's AI boom poured fuel on Delta's top and bottom lines.
Delta's corporate sales grew by double-digit percentages across all sectors, particularly those tied to AI, as execs from exposed industries likely traveled more to close deals, raise money, and visit data center sites.
"Corporate sales growth was led by the banking, technology, and energy sectors, with particularly strong performance in Boston and Los Angeles," Delta said.
Read more: Find the best travel credit cards for free flights, hotel stays, and more
Boston is a well-known financial services hub, while Los Angeles is a great landing spot for entering the tech ecosystem.
Despite the apparent AI-related momentum, Delta had a challenging third quarter amid surging fuel prices.
The Ed Bastian-led airline saw second quarter earnings land at $1.72 a share, below analyst forecasts for $1.82 a share. Delta called out a $500 million higher fuel bill compared to the guidance it offered in July.
Fuel expenses rose by $1.78 billion year over year, or 69%.
The company issued fourth quarter earnings per share guidance in a range of $1.15 to $1.65, well below consensus estimates. The Street was looking for $1.42.
Delta stock fell 1% in premarket trading.

item.title: Delta reports Q3 earnings miss, cuts guidance as fuel costs surge 62% from year ago
item.author: Pras Subramanian
item.description:
Delta reports Q3 earnings miss, cuts guidance as fuel costs surge 62% from year ago
2026-10-11
Por Pras Subramanian
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/delta-reports-q3-earnings-miss-cuts-guidance-as-fuel-costs-surge-62-from-year-ago-103121231.html
Delta Air Lines (DAL) reported third quarter results on Friday morning that missed the mark, as strength from Delta's premium business could not blunt the effects of higher fuel prices. Delta subsequently cut its guidance, noting that its total fuel bill for the year would increase by a whopping $6 billion.
For the quarter, Delta reported Q3 adjusted revenue of $17.58 billion, slightly below analyst estimates of $17.76 billion per Bloomberg, up 15.7% from a year ago. Delta posted adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $1.72 vs. the $1.82 estimate, and adjusted net income of $1.134 billion vs. the $1.23 billion expected.
Delta said its Q3 performance was hit by $500 million in higher fuel costs than the guidance it issued in July. Delta's total fuel bill for the quarter hit $4.1 billion, up 62% from a year ago, as the US-Israeli war with Iran rocked the global oil market.
Read more: How oil price shocks ripple through your wallet, from gas to groceries
Delta stock was down over 1% in premarket trading.
Speaking of guidance, Delta cut its adjusted EPS forecast to $5.10-$5.60 from $6.50-$7.50, with its free cash flow forecast coming down to $2.5 billion from a range of $3 billion to $4 billion.
"For the full year, we expect to generate a pre-tax profit of roughly $4.5 billion, absorbing a $6 billion increase in fuel costs," CEO Ed Bastian said in a statement. "Looking ahead, our focus remains on profitable growth and delivering against our long-term financial framework, including mid-teens margins and returns, durable free cash flow, and gross leverage of approximately one times."
"All of it's fuel," CFO Erik Snell added when asked where the impact of the guidance cut came from on a call with reporters. Snell added that he expects fuel costs to be higher next quarter as well, but Delta is planning to grow capacity by 2%, a reversal from earlier this year.
It was Delta's highest-spending customers who helped blunt some of the blow this quarter.
Delta's premium business grew 18% year over year in Q3, with loyalty and related revenue up 18% as well. American Express (AXP) credit card remuneration grew 15% from a year ago, on track to "exceed $9 billion" for the year, Delta said.
Read more: Delta SkyMiles Gold American Express Card review
Part of the reason Delta's premium segment is so strong is the perceived benefits of higher service and better loyalty treatment that Delta's SkyMiles members expect. However, one area that's been a thorn in the airline's side is in-flight wifi.

item.title: Four signs it is about to get uglier in the bond market as yields rise
item.author: Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss; Suzanne McGee; Laura Matthews
item.description:
Four signs it is about to get uglier in the bond market as yields rise
2026-10-11
Por Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss; Suzanne McGee; Laura Matthews
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/options/articles/four-signs-uglier-bond-market-100537045.html
By Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss, Suzanne McGee and Laura Matthews
NEW YORK, Oct 9 (Reuters) - It is white-knuckle time in the bond market.
US Treasury yields have risen sharply since the war with Iran began in February, with the 10-year yield up some 135 basis points to 5.23% and the 30-year yield up around 110 basis points from its March low to 5.614%. Both are trading at levels last seen more than two decades ago.
Investors are watching whether bond selling is starting to create its own momentum. Some key technical measures suggest another surge to even-higher yields could be ahead, creating a feedback loop that amplifies the market stress, though there are also reasons to believe that buyers will soon step in, seeking to lock in yields at their most investor-friendly levels since George W. Bush was president.
"People in the market are recalibrating their expectations," said Dustin Reid, fixed income strategist at Mackenzie Investments.
Here are four signs that the selling could worsen.
VOLATILITY IS RISING IN RATE OPTIONS
Investors are seeking out protection against rising yields, referred to as the "payer skew," in the options market. Investors use these markets to insure their portfolios against a sharp move in yields without having to sell their Treasury holdings.
Demand for short-term protection against a jump in 10-year US swap rates has intensified, pushing the cost of insuring against a 200-basis-point rate rise over the next three months to 132 bps on Monday, the highest since the March 2023 banking crisis triggered by the collapse of Silicon Valley Bank.
Swap rates refer to the cost investors pay to lock in a fixed interest rate instead of paying a floating rate.
While options are tied to swap rates rather than Treasury yields, the two typically move together, making the surge in payer skew an indication of concern about the risk of higher long-term Treasury yields.
Implied volatility, a key input in option prices, has climbed to 21.4 basis points for one-month options on 10-year swap rates, the highest since late March, reflecting growing uncertainty over the path of long-term yields.
AI BUILDOUT RESHAPES CREDIT MARKETS
A major contributor to the selloff has been a surge in corporate issuance to support the AI buildout, investors said. Spreads have remained tight, but buyers of longer-term bonds issued by AI hyperscalers are using the Treasury market to hedge their duration risk, a measure of exposure to rising interest rates — a practice that lately has spurred selling.
"When a transaction prices midday, in the afternoon everyone is selling Treasury futures," said Neil Sun, portfolio manager at RBC BlueBay Asset Management, who focuses on investment-grade credit. Those who aren't hedging sometimes sell Treasuries outright to make room for higher-yielding investment-grade bonds.
Goldman Sachs predicts that hyperscalers could sell a record $420 billion in debt next year, which likely means more hedging or selling of government securities.
MORTGAGE HEDGING IS GATHERING PACE
Investors exposed to mortgage assets are also hedging against the selloff in Treasuries. As rates rise, the expected life of mortgage-backed securities extends, making them more sensitive to further moves in yields in what is known as duration risk.
Investors often respond by increasing interest-rate hedges to offset that added duration risk, a process known as convexity hedging. That includes selling of Treasury futures — which can add to selling pressure across bond markets.
"The market is carrying a substantial cohort of mortgages originated over the past three years at coupons relatively close to current mortgage rates," said Mike Riddle, chief executive officer at Eris Innovations, a Chica
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: The case for hardware in the AI era is getting more compelling
item.author: Hamza Shaban
item.description:
The case for hardware in the AI era is getting more compelling
2026-10-11
Por Hamza Shaban
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/the-case-for-hardware-in-the-ai-era-is-getting-more-compelling-100000428.html
The term now seems almost quaint, the "iPhone killer."
For almost two decades, tech companies have attempted to dethrone the king of gadgets without success. The phone market has since matured, and consumers have their pick that's been so "good enough" that Apple (AAPL) struggles to convince people to upgrade.
What's urgently driving the tech world now isn't an effort to directly subvert the smartphone but to find novel ways to package AI into old and new hardware.
And the case for doing it is becoming more persuasive.
Apple itself is getting in on the action. As with its lock on apps and services, Cupertino acts as an innovative landlord, extracting rents. And, as Yorkville Ives's Dan Ives put it, the company is looking to extend that strategy as "the toll collector on the consumer AI highway."
"Much of the debate has centered on whether Apple arrived early or late to generative AI," he wrote in a note earlier this week. "We think the question that matters more is how well the company can put useful AI in front of an installed base of more than 2.5 billion active devices and 1.5 billion iPhones."
For any AI-infused device, trust will be key. And that's where Apple shines. While the new generation of AI labs wrestles with muddy debates about safety, mass unemployment, security vulnerabilities, and misuse, Apple has quietly gone about its business, burnishing its reputation.
No rogue AI agents or apocalyptic AI takeovers here. Just an upgraded Siri that everyone has been waiting for, and more ways to use apps that you already rely upon to get things done.
In a roundabout way, new AI-powered hardware might be the catalyst to weaken the dominance of the smartphone as the be-all and end-all consumer form factor.
Microsoft this week unveiled its Nvidia-powered Surface Laptop Ultra, designed to let users run AI models at home without relying on the cloud. That's another pathway for AI hardware to succeed. The idea of running your own micro-data center at home might not be for everyone, but it has a certain appeal when you look at how much AI can cost on the cloud.
Rather than use an online AI service, you can instead load an app on your computer, download the model of your choice, and get busy — essentially for the cost of your computer and power bill. For consumers and professionals whose main concern is maintaining privacy in the AI era, running a capable machine of your own has special appeal.
But perhaps Apple will join Microsoft in doing this, and maybe the iPhone will still be the point guard for a person's DIY AI model at home.

https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/the-case-for-hardware-in-the-ai-era-is-getting-more-compelling-100000428.html

The term now seems almost quaint, the "iPhone killer."

For almost two decades, tech companies have attempted to dethrone the king of gadgets without success. The phone market has since matured, and consumers have their pick that's been so "good enough" that Apple (AAPL) struggles to convince people to upgrade.

What's urgently driving the tech world now isn't an effort to directly subvert the smartphone but to find novel ways to package AI into old and new hardware.

And the case for doing it is becoming more persuasive.

Apple itself is getting in on the action. As with its lock on apps and services, Cupertino acts as an innovative landlord, extracting rents. And, as Yorkville Ives's Dan Ives put it, the company is looking to extend that strategy as "the toll collector on the consumer AI highway."

"Much of the debate has centered on whether Apple arrived early or late to generative AI," he wrote in a note earlier this week. "We think the question that matters more is how well the company can put useful AI in front of an installed base of more than 2.5 billion active devices and 1.5 billion iPhones."

For any AI-infused device, trust will be key. And that's where Apple shines. While the new generation of AI labs wrestles with muddy debates about safety, mass unemployment, security vulnerabilities, and misuse, Apple has quietly gone about its business, burnishing its reputation.

No rogue AI agents or apocalyptic AI takeovers here. Just an upgraded Siri that everyone has been waiting for, and more ways to use apps that you already rely upon to get things done.

In a roundabout way, new AI-powered hardware might be the catalyst to weaken the dominance of the smartphone as the be-all and end-all consumer form factor.

Microsoft this week unveiled its Nvidia-powered Surface Laptop Ultra, designed to let users run AI models at home without relying on the cloud. That's another pathway for AI hardware to succeed. The idea of running your own micro-data center at home might not be for everyone, but it has a certain appeal when you look at how much AI can cost on the cloud.

Rather than use an online AI service, you can instead load an app on your computer, download the model of your choice, and get busy — essentially for the cost of your computer and power bill. For consumers and professionals whose main concern is maintaining privacy in the AI era, running a capable machine of your own has special appeal.

But perhaps Apple will join Microsoft in doing this, and maybe the iPhone will still be the point guard for a person's DIY AI model at home.

item.title: Consumer sentiment falls to 5-month low as frustration mounts over higher costs
item.author: Brooke DiPalma
item.description:
Consumer sentiment falls to 5-month low as frustration mounts over higher costs
2026-10-11
Por Brooke DiPalma
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/article/consumer-sentiment-falls-to-5-month-low-as-frustration-mounts-over-higher-costs-143114047.html
Consumer sentiment fell in October as frustration over the higher cost of living weighed on Americans' views of the economy, according to a survey from the University of Michigan.
Overall consumer sentiment fell to 46.3 in October, down 1.8 points from September's reading of 48.1. The preliminary reading was slightly below Wall Street's expectation of 47.3.
"Frustration over cost-of-living continues to mount, as consumers across the political spectrum believe that the trajectory of the economy has weakened since the beginning of the year," Joanne Hsu, the survey's director, said in the release.
With 25 days until the midterm elections, Hsu added that sentiment among Democrats and Republicans improved, but that was offset by a decline in independents.
Read more: What is consumer confidence, and why does it matter?
Consumers face a growing number of macroeconomic concerns: Higher inflation; worries over the US national debt, which is now above $40 trillion; and a rise in the benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield (^TNX), which risks jumping to 6% for the first time since 2000. The 10-year yield is often a gauge for global borrowing costs, and its recent increase has dampened Americans' outlook for buying conditions.
This week, the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate increased to 7.4%, a three-year high, according to Freddie Mac survey data.
Sentiment among groups who have fewer resources to weather price increases, such as lower-income consumers and those with smaller stock portfolios, declined this month.
As consumer prices rise and the war with Iran continues, Americans' outlook for inflation in the year ahead ticked up to 4.7% this month from 4.6% last month.
Inflation expectations were far higher than the 3.4% rate recorded in February, when the war in the Middle East and its subsequent energy shock began.
Gas prices have increased by more than $1.50 on average since the beginning of the war, according to AAA, and have stayed elevated above $4 since midsummer.
Long-term inflation expectations increased to 3.5% this month, a tick higher than the 3.4% reading in September. In recent months, they have consistently remained above the 2.8%-3.2% range seen in 2024.
Brooke DiPalma is a reporter for Yahoo Finance. Follow her on X at @BrookeDiPalma or email her at bdipalma@yahoofinance.com.

item.title: Trump forms committee to investigate mortgage fraud allegations against Fed governor Lisa Cook
item.author: Jennifer Schonberger
item.description:
Trump forms committee to investigate mortgage fraud allegations against Fed governor Lisa Cook
2026-10-11
Por Jennifer Schonberger
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/trump-forms-committee-to-investigate-mortgage-fraud-allegations-against-fed-governor-lisa-cook-153243615.html
President Trump has established a committee to investigate allegations against Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook, including mortgage fraud and whether her statements constituted legal "cause" for Cook's removal from the central bank.
The president has tasked the committee with investigating whether Cook made false statements about two mortgages she took out. The group will report to him whether there is legal cause for Cook's removal.
Trump fired Cook, the first Black woman to serve as a Fed governor, in August 2025, claiming she committed mortgage fraud by making misrepresentations on loan documents years before her appointment to the central bank. Cook, a Biden appointee, has denied any wrongdoing and sued. The lawsuit has gone through multiple court rungs before reaching the Supreme Court earlier this year.
The Supreme Court ruled in June that Cook can continue serving on the Fed's Board of Governors, but did not rule on the merits of mortgage fraud allegations.
Section 10 of the Federal Reserve Act states that each member of the board shall hold office for 14 years unless sooner removed for cause by the president. The statute does not detail what constitutes "for cause." That term has been interpreted in legal rulings to mean inefficiency, neglect of duty, or malfeasance.
In a memo released Friday, the president instructed the committee to conduct an in-person hearing on Nov. 5 to consider the evidence and allegations against Cook. The hearing is set to take place at the White House.
"We have grave doubts that this 'hearing' is a legitimate one that would conform to the law," Abbe Lowell and Norm Eisen, lawyers representing Cook, said in a statement. "But if it is anything close to objective, the conclusion will be that Governor Cook did not commit mortgage fraud, leaving no cause to remove her from the Federal Reserve Board."
Cook's lawyers said they have engaged with the White House to evaluate whether the proposed process is genuine and not simply a "box-checking exercise."
The memo states that Cook may submit a written position statement to the committee regarding the allegations at least three days before the hearing and a post-hearing written statement by Nov. 10.
"As soon as practicable after receipt of that statement, the Committee shall submit written findings of fact and conclusions of law to me and shall recommend whether there is cause to remove Governor Cook from her position on the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve," Trump's memo states.
The assistant to the president for economic policy, the chair of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, and the director of the Office of Government Ethics will serve as members of the committee.

item.title: Healthcare's Next Growth Drivers
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
Healthcare's Next Growth Drivers
2026-10-09
Por Texto propio
Healthcare's Next Growth Drivers
Key Takeaways
Healthcare leaders are navigating policy uncertainty, future patent expirations and intensifying global competition for innovation.
Healthcare M&A remains resilient, with strategic buyers pursuing innovation, scale and pipeline growth opportunities.
Biopharma companies are investing heavily in areas such as oncology, obesity and next-generation diagnostics to fuel future growth.
AI is helping companies accelerate drug discovery, streamline operations and improve patient engagement.
As healthcare leaders and investors gathered at the 2026 Morgan Stanley Global Healthcare Conference, conversations centered on an industry balancing innovation, growth and disruption. Morgan Stanley bankers highlighted a stronger financing environment in biotech, robust demand for differentiated therapies and technologies and the growing importance of data and AI across healthcare. Executives also discussed advances in oncology and obesity, the outlook for healthcare M&A and the growing role of Chinese biotech in the global innovation ecosystem.
We've seen breakout clinical data sets, very strong drug launches and the most robust biotech M&A market in many years.
James Talbot
Co-Head of EMEA Healthcare Investment Banking
Underlying many of the panel discussions was a rapidly evolving industry backdrop. Executives weighed the implications of the upcoming U.S. midterm elections, including the future of PBM reform, which could reshape the role of prescription-drug intermediaries, and 340B reform, which could affect drug pricing and provider reimbursement. Many discussions also focused on China's growing role in drug discovery, both as a source of innovation and an increasingly important partner, while raising questions about how companies can maintain a competitive edge and accelerate the path from scientific discovery to patient care.
The following themes stood out for company leaders and investors:
Healthcare M&A's continued momentum, driven largely by strategic acquirers seeking innovation and scale.
Investing for the next wave of growth, from oncology and obesity to cell therapy and next-generation diagnostics.
AI's growing influence across healthcare, from drug discovery and clinical development to commercialization, patient care and capital allocation decisions.
Healthcare M&A's Continued Momentum
At a panel featuring Morgan Stanley healthcare M&A bankers, discussion centered on the durability of the current deal environment and what is driving activity across the sector. Despite a more challenging backdrop in some areas of healthcare, panelists remained constructive on the outlook. Annualized global announced M&A volume has reached approximately $4.7 trillion, well above the $3.2 trillion average for 2016 to 2025, while announced volume for transactions valued at $10 billion or more is up 57% year to date. Strategic acquirers, rather than financial sponsors, continue to drive much of the momentum, with biopharma accounting for roughly 70% of healthcare deal activity.
Pharma’s need for innovation and growth isn’t going away. Biotech remains a critical part of the solution.
David Haber
Managing Director, Healthcare Investment Banking
Biopharma remains at the center of dealmaking. Panelists pointed to a wave of patent expirations expected later this decade. Panelists noted that many pharmaceutical companies face significant revenue headwinds in the years ahead, creating a need for both internal innovation and external growth. As a result, buyers continue to pursue assets that can strengthen pipelines and expand into attractive therapeutic areas, with both large pharmaceutical companies and increasingly active mid-cap biopharma companies participating in the market.
At the same time, competition for high-quality assets is intensifying. Improved capital markets have given biotech companies more flexibility to remain ind

item.title: China’s New Era of Manufacturing
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
China’s New Era of Manufacturing
2026-10-09
Por Texto propio
China’s New Era of Manufacturing
Key Takeaways
As global supply chains evolve, China's role may shift from "made in China" to "made by China," with its technologies and industrial capabilities increasingly embedded in manufacturing worldwide.
AI is moving beyond standalone tools and becoming embedded across factories, supply chains and industrial systems.
China's Industry 5.0 strategy could unlock $12 trillion in investment over the next decade.
The largest opportunities span factory upgrades, automation, robotics, semiconductors and industrial software.
China is entering a new phase of its decades-long industrial evolution — one that could reshape manufacturing and productivity worldwide.
“China is moving from being the world’s factory toward becoming the world’s industrial operating system – combining scale, automation, AI, supply-chain depth and global deployment,” says Sheng Zhong, Morgan Stanley’s Head of China Industrials Research.
Unlike previous industrial revolutions centered primarily on technological progress, China's Industry 5.0 is simultaneously a productivity revolution, a geopolitical response, a manufacturing reorganization and a strategic capital Supercycle.
Sheng Zhong
Morgan Stanley’s Head of China Industrials Research
Morgan Stanley Research believes this shift from “made in China” to “made by China” could help China capture more value in higher-margin areas such as software, advanced equipment and industrial technology, supporting an increase in profit margins from approximately 5% to 8% and increasing China’s share of global manufacturing value-added from 28% to 30% by 2035.

item.title: Cambios introduce Ley Reformatoria al Código Tributario aprobada en Ecuador
item.author: Pérez Bustamante; Ponce
item.description:
Cambios introduce Ley Reformatoria al Código Tributario aprobada en Ecuador
2026-10-09
Por Pérez Bustamante; Ponce
https://www.pbplaw.com/publicaciones/qué-cambios-introduce-la-ley-reformatoria-al-código-tributario-aprobada-por-la-asamblea-nacional/
Asamblea Nacional aprueba el Proyecto de Ley Orgánica Reformatoria al Código Tributario
Con 83 votos a favor, 60 en contra y 3 abstenciones, el Pleno de la Asamblea Nacional aprobó este martes 6 de octubre de 2026, el Proyecto de Ley Orgánica Reformatoria al Código Tributario. El Proyecto pasará a la revisión del Presidente de la República, y en caso de sanción, será publicado en el Registro Oficial.
El Proyecto plantea importantes reformas al Código Tributario, así como a la Ley de Régimen Tributario Interno.
¿Cuáles son los principales cambios?
En el Código Tributario de 1975, se introducen los siguientes cambios:
Reformas generales
- Se agrega un nuevo derecho del contribuyente: los cambios de criterio interpretativo de alcance general tendrán que publicarse en una norma, y regirán solo hacia el futuro, salvo que sean más favorables.
- Se aclara que el Código Tributario tiene la naturaleza de ley orgánica.
- Se actualiza la denominación de los tribunales fiscales por "Tribunales Distritales de lo Contencioso Tributario", denominación que mantienen desde la expedición del Código Orgánico de la Función Judicial en 2009.
Reformas relativas al valor de los actos normativos de la administración tributaria
- Se puntualiza que las circulares obligarán solo a los funcionarios y no serán vinculantes para los contribuyentes.
- Se dispone que las fichas técnicas, manuales, instructivos y criterios internos de las administraciones tributarias, no podrán crear, modificar ni extinguir obligaciones, exenciones ni beneficios.
Reformas relativas a notificaciones
- Se aclara que la Administración tendrá que usar primero el medio de notificación que el contribuyente haya señalado en el expediente (por ejemplo, correo o casillero judicial) y se dispone que solo podrá usar otro medio si existe una imposibilidad técnica justificada.
- Se precisa que la notificación electrónica se hará por el buzón del contribuyente y por los correos que este haya señalado.
Sobre las solicitudes, reclamos y la determinación complementaria
- Se aclara que los sujetos pasivos pueden presentar reclamos contra todo tipo de actos administrativos emanados de las administraciones tributarias (actualmente el Código se refiere solamente a “actos determinativos”.
- Se aclara que la determinación complementaria es un proceso que puede iniciarse únicamente en el trámite de reclamos (no de solicitudes).
- Aunque se mantiene el plazo de 120 días hábiles desde el día siguiente a la presentación como término para la resolución de reclamos, se clarifica que las solicitudes de información que se realicen en el trámite de los mismos, tendrán que hacerse dentro de 60 días y se dispone que la suspensión que puede ordenarse por este motivo, en ningún caso podrá superar 90 días ni ocurrir más de una vez.
- Respecto a la solicitudes de devolución de pago en exceso, se dispone que el término para resolverlas será de 120 días (actualmente se establece un plazo de 6 meses) y en caso de negativa, se aclara que el sujeto pasivo acudir directamente a las acciones judiciales del COGEP.
Sobre el recurso de revisión
Se dispone que si el interesado presenta el recurso, la Administración estará obligada a admitirlo, tramitarlo y emitir una resolución motivada. Hoy se trata como una facultad potestativa de la administración.
- Se fijan requisitos de admisibilidad:
Los mismos exigidos para la presentación del reclamo, conforme al artículo 119 del Código Tributario; y además:
- - La determinación de las causales en que se funda.
- - El anuncio probatorio, cuando corresponda.
- Si el escrito que contiene el recurso de revisión es oscuro o incompleto, se concede 10 días para aclararlo o completarlo.
- Se modifican los plazos d

item.title: As mortgage rates rise, more borrowers are turning to adjustable-rate loans
item.author: Claire Boston
item.description:
As mortgage rates rise, more borrowers are turning to adjustable-rate loans
2026-10-09
Por Claire Boston
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/as-mortgage-rates-rise-more-borrowers-are-turning-to-adjustable-rate-loans-171507956.html
As mortgage rates approach 8%, more buyers are turning to adjustable-rate mortgages to save on interest.
Nearly 11% of mortgage borrowers who locked in a rate in mid-September opted for an ARM, according to ICE Mortgage Technology data. The share is up more than three percentage points over the past three months to the highest in nearly four years.
ARMs can offer meaningful rate savings over a 30-year fixed-rate loan, but there's a catch: Instead of locking in one rate for the entire 30-year term, borrowers commit to an initial, often lower rate for a shorter period, typically five or seven years. After the initial term is up, their rate adjusts based on market conditions once or twice a year.
Read more: How to get the lowest mortgage rates right now
In the chart above, "rate lock activity" refers to borrowers locking in a rate after applying for a mortgage. Refinancings are leading the trend, likely driven by owners who took out a fixed-rate loan above 7% and those needing to cash out some of their equity.
Many borrowers think the rate gamble is worth it: While the average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage is around 7.63% on Wednesday, a 7/6 ARM — which carries a fixed term for seven years and then adjusts every six months — is 6.95%, according to Mortgage News Daily.
Many borrowers who seek out ARMs intend to sell their home before their initial fixed-rate term expires. Others are effectively betting that rates will be lower in the future, allowing them to refinance.
Most borrowers who took out ARMs in 2022 and 2023, when rates first started moving higher, remain in their initial fixed-rate period, meaning the Fed's recent tightening hasn't affected their rates. While 30-year fixed mortgage rates aren't directly influenced by the Fed, ARMs in their adjustment rates are much more sensitive to the central bank's interest rate decisions.
Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

item.title: Por qué lo de diario Expreso es muy grave
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
Por qué lo de diario Expreso es muy grave
2026-10-09
Por Texto propio
Por qué lo de diario Expreso es muy grave
Carlos Rojas
October 7, 2026
Si bien la prensa ecuatoriana vivió entre 2007 y 2017 una política sistemática de amedrentamiento y silenciamiento, todos los medios independientes estaban unidos defendiendo principios que hoy importan a muy pocos.
1.- Porque igual a cómo sucedió con Rafael Correa, hace diez años, se reedita una peligrosa pelea entre el gobierno de turno, intolerante a la crítica y la fiscalización, y la prensa independiente, pilar de cualquier democracia liberal.
2.- Porque el tránsito que irremediablemente debe dar un medio tradicional hacia formatos digitales es muy complejo y costoso, por lo que las presiones políticas, judiciales y financieras externas restan oxígeno y fuerza a ese momento.
3.- Porque si bien la prensa ecuatoriana vivió entre 2007 y 2017 una política sistemática de amedrentamiento y silenciamiento, todos los medios independientes estaban unidos defendiendo principios que hoy importan a muy pocos. Decenas de periodistas y líderes de opinión que años atrás libraron una verdadera batalla por las libertades hoy callan, acomodados al financiamiento que el poder decidió otorgarles a cambio de su obsecuencia.
4.- Porque el papel de las élites, en especial de los empresarios, luce apagado, desorientado y sin entender que los referentes democráticos son esenciales para el desarrollo nacional. Y allí el patrocinio del trabajo de la prensa libre es fundamental.
5.- Porque a la gente, en general, parece preocuparle muy poco que el espacio de la prensa independiente esté cada vez más reducido, mientras las falencias institucionales y de gestión del Gobierno ameritan amplios espacios de fiscalización.
Lo que está ocurriendo con diario Expreso es un síntoma muy grave de que la salud democrática del Ecuador anda mal. Empeora.

2026-10-09

Por Texto propio

Por qué lo de diario Expreso es muy grave

Carlos Rojas

October 7, 2026

Si bien la prensa ecuatoriana vivió entre 2007 y 2017 una política sistemática de amedrentamiento y silenciamiento, todos los medios independientes estaban unidos defendiendo principios que hoy importan a muy pocos.

item.title: María Paz Jervis tenía razon
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
María Paz Jervis tenía razon
2026-10-09
Por Texto propio
Empresarios: María Paz Jervis tenía razón
Carlos Rojas
October 2, 2026
Es una lástima que un país los industriales y empresarios no logren tener una posición clara, respetuosa, digna y firme frente a un gobierno cuyas decisiones los afecta profundamente.
En el marco de la celebración por los 90 años de la CIP, María Paz Jervis dijo sentirse sorprendida y desesperanzada por ver a un sector empresarial “con tanto miedo”. Miedo -insistió- a defender la libertad de expresión, los valores democráticos y a pensar que disentir con las decisiones que toma el Gobierno no es convertirse en enemigos.
Estas declaraciones, que cayeron muy mal en todo el gremio a escala nacional, se dieron a la par de las disposiciones del Ministerio de Energía para que las grandes industrias tengan un día de desconexión eléctrica.
El alboroto que se desató en redes sociales coincidió con la renuncia de Jervis a la presidencia de la Cámara, mientras en los canales de televisión y las redes sociales, otros dirigentes de este sector decían que es mejor tener un diálogo constructivo con el Régimen pues la crisis energética debe ser resuelta con el apoyo de todos.
No faltaron las críticas a Jervis de parte los periodistas-voceros del Ejecutivo, aquellos que, desde sus radios, justifican cada una de las decisiones del Presidente, al punto de que sus comentarios terminan convertidos en verdaderas tomaduras de pelo para sus audiencias. Claro, celebraban la renuncia de la dirigente como la consecuencia natural de lo que calificaron como un error de bulto: hablar por los empresarios bajo criterios que eran únicamente suyos.
Tres doritos después, la cruda realidad meteorológica y el inconmovible pragmatismo del presidente Noboa demostraron que Jervis no estaba del todo equivocada. Es decir, que el temor no garantiza un buen trato.
En seis días, la orden de desconexión pasó de un día a tres por semana; y en Durán, el racionamiento para las grandes industrias será de cuatro.
Al inicio, el plan del Ministerio de Energía era afectar a 182 de esas empresas, pero para el viernes subieron a casi nueve mil. Como si esto no fuera suficiente, hasta les incrementaron de forma drástica la tarifa eléctrica.
Semejante paquetazo obligó a la Cámara de Industrias de Guayaquil, primero, y a la que presidía Jervis, después, a emitir sendos comunicados que tendrán cero efectos reales, ante un Régimen que no está acostumbrado a retroceder.
Es una lástima que un país donde los industriales y empresarios quisieron tumbar a Osvaldo Hurtado; marcaron el ascenso político e influyeron con sus tesis en el gobierno de Febres Cordero; o arrinconaron a Bucaram, Mahuad y Gutiérrez en sus horas difíciles, sean hoy incapaces de tener una posición clara, respetuosa, digna y firme frente a un gobierno que preferirá apagar a todo el sector productivo creyendo que con ello no cortará la luz de los millones de hogares en vísperas de unas elecciones donde el poder político de ADN está en juego. La ingenuidad de los empresarios le costará algunos puntos del PIB.

item.title: Mala semana para Daniel Noboa
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
Mala semana para Daniel Noboa
2026-10-09
Por Texto propio
Mala semana para Daniel Noboa
By Carlos Rojas
October 9, 2026
Al Presidente le hicieron cometer tremendo error, el lunes a primera hora, cuando prometió públicamente en una de las radios, cuya línea editorial está bajo su control, que no habría apagones en los hogares ecuatorianos.
El presidente Daniel Noboa durante el evento por la Independencia de Guayaquil en el Coliseo Voltaire Paladines Polo. Foto: API
El presidente Daniel Noboa durante el evento por la Independencia de Guayaquil en el Coliseo Voltaire Paladines Polo. Foto: API
Cuando los asesores de un presidente construyen la estrategia política de su gobierno sobre la base de un espejismo, se exponen a que esta, más temprano que tarde, se invalide al primer choque con la realidad.
A Daniel Noboa le hicieron cometer tremendo error, el lunes a primera hora, cuando prometió públicamente en una de las radios, cuya línea editorial está bajo su control, que no habría apagones en los hogares ecuatorianos. La frase fue replicada por el aparato comunicacional de todo Carondelet.
Han pasado casi tres años de mandato, así como tres crisis eléctricas, y en el Ejecutivo no aprenden la lecció n. La realidad no se teje a punta de propaganda ni de deseos formulados sobre la base del capricho. Este jueves, final de una semana corta, los ecuatorianos se van al feriado con una sensación de incertidumbre total, pues las grandes y medianas industrias se desconectarán tres días por semana, cuando el compromiso del Ministerio de Energía, el viernes anterior, era de que los apagones solo fueran de dos días.
Y lo más complejo, el martes en Guayaquil y este día en Quito, varios sectores de ambas urbes han reportado cortes no programados de electricidad, mientras las pantallas de la Celec muestran el caudal de Mazar cayendo en picada.
Con miles de hogares sin luz en ciertas horas pico de la demanda, así la autoridad eléctrica diga que es por mantenimiento de las redes de transmisión o por el daño en alguna estación, lo único que conseguirá el Gobierno es que la gente ponga en duda la promesa del Presidente y su palabra se devalúe.
Los asesores, funcionarios y periodistas áulicos de su despacho hacen mal en insertar al Jefe de Estado en un mundo paralelo, que nada tiene que ver con la realidad que, por otro lado, y por más adversa que esta sea, la prensa retrata todos los días, así la califiquen de odiadora, mala fe o negativa.
Esa desesperación porque la gente mastique sin ningún reparo estas narrativas contradice el supuesto buen momento por el que pasa Noboa según las encuestas (hasta casi 20 puntos, supuestamente recuperados en dos meses).
Tampoco se entiende la desacertada carta que el mandatario difundió la mañana del miércoles 7 de octubre, anunciando que el galón de la Extra, Ecopaís y el diésel bajará cuatro centavos, pese que la economía global tiene que lidiar con un petróleo y sus derivados que están por las nubes.
¿Para qué el Presidente se ancla a anuncios tan controversiales si se supone que todo va bien con su popularidad?
Esa sobrerreacción comunicacional llama la atención sobre manera. Noboa no tardó en colgar en sus redes un video muy corto sobre las obras que tiene para la Universidad de Cuenca, pocas horas después de que los estudiantes lo recibieran mal en su visita a ese centro académico el miércoles.
O que Julio José Neira pusiera todo su talento -que no es mucho, por cierto- a cuestionar el reportaje de Ecuavisa sobre la construcción del hospital del IESS en Cayambe donde, lejos del render propagandístico, apenas hay algún movimiento de tierras.
En fin, esta semana cierra de muy mala manera para un gobierno acostumbrado a los golpes de efecto diarios, pero descuidando el panorama real. Por eso los tropiezos.

item.title: La trampa de las encuestas
item.author: Texto propio
item.description:
La trampa de las encuestas
2026-10-09
Por Texto propio
La trampa de las encuestas
Por Carlos Rojas
October 6, 2026
Gobernar desde la percepción de las encuestas siempre será un error para cualquier político, tanto en Brasil como Ecuador, donde el voto oculto es un mecanismo de defensa frente al autoritarismo.
Hasta el domingo en la mañana, buena parte de América Latina intuía que Lula da Silva iba a vencer en la primera vuelta y proyectar así la consolidación de su triunfo en la balotaje del 24 de octubre próximo.
Pero su rival, el ultraderechista Flavio Bolsonaro le aguó la fiesta pues, por momentos, parecía que iba a ganar la presidencia en una sola elección.

Good morning. The major averages retreated for a second day in a row, with chip stocks falling.
Long-dated bonds climbed again, and Brent crude oil futures (BZ=F) rose toward $105 per barrel amid persistent US-Iran tensions.
The 10-year Treasury (^TNX) yield rose to 5.32%, signaling a tightening of financial conditions as everything from mortgages to car loans and corporate borrowing becomes more expensive.
The market forecasts the Federal Reserve will keep rates unchanged at its October meeting, but raise them in December.

Here's a check of the markets in the first few minutes of trading, based on a heat map powered by Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data.
Tech (XLK) stocks slipped, with AI chip giants Nvidia (NVDA) and AMD (AMD) set to decline from their record highs for a second day in a row.
South Korean memory maker Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) reported a preliminary record third quarter profit of $80 billion, but the forecast did little to lift the rest of the chip sector, with peers Micron (MU) and SK Hynix (SKHY) trading lower.
Bitcoin (BTC-USD) declined to trade below $83,000 per token.
Here are some other notable stocks that Yahoo Finance readers are viewing this morning: Palentir (PLTR), PepsiCo (PEP), and Applied Digital (APLD).

item.title: AMD CEO Lisa Su just struck another bullish note with the stock on fire
item.author: Brian Sozzi
item.description:
AMD CEO Lisa Su just struck another bullish note with the stock on fire
2026-10-09
Por Brian Sozzi
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/amd-ceo-lisa-su-just-struck-another-bullish-note-with-the-stock-on-fire-101318248.html
AMD (AMD) CEO Lisa Su is dropping bullish nuggets all over the place on her overseas chip tour.
On a visit to Seoul on Wednesday to meet with the likes of Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix (SKHY), Su said overall data center demand remained "very strong," according to a Reuters report. Su reportedly added that she is seeing "strong demand signals" across AMD's product portfolio.
This comes a day after a trip to Taipei on Tuesday, where she predicted chip demand would stay strong for years.
Shares of AMD are trading at a record high and are up 200% year to date.
The stock has more record highs ahead, in part because of demand for the new Meta (META) AI agent known as Muse, Citi said on Tuesday.
Citi analyst Atif Malik raised his price target on AMD to $800 from $575.
"Following the release of Meta Muse and our subsequent CPU TAM raise, we are raising estimates on AMD given our belief that AMD will be the primary beneficiary of the CPU renaissance and our belief that Meta is one of the largest customers of AMD's server business," Malik said.
Malik also struck a bullish tone on the future size of the CPU market.
"We update our CPU model post the launch of Muse, Meta's personal AI agent. Fundamentally, we view agentic AI as a potential orders-of-magnitude driver of compute demand relative to traditional chatbots," Malik added. "We believe the CPU TAM [total addressable market] expands from $29 billion in 2025 to $300 billion in 2030, or a 60% CAGR. We still expect AMD to be the key beneficiary of the CPU renaissance and Intel as a secondary beneficiary."

item.title: The tech industry wants you to run AI models at home, but it’s not for everyone
item.author: Daniel Howley
item.description:
The tech industry wants you to run AI models at home, but it’s not for everyone
2026-10-09
Por Daniel Howley
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/article/the-tech-industry-wants-you-to-run-ai-models-at-home-but-its-not-for-everyone-195314548.html
Microsoft (MSFT) on Wednesday unveiled its Nvidia-powered Surface Laptop Ultra, designed to let users run AI models at home without relying on the cloud.
Starting at $2,599, the Surface Laptop Ultra runs on Nvidia's (NVDA) Arm-based RTX Spark, which offers upwards of 128GB of onboard memory.
Most consumers and enterprise users access AI platforms through cloud services like OpenAI's (OPAI.PVT) ChatGPT, Anthropic's (ANTH.PVT) Claude, Google's (GOOG, GOOGL) Gemini, or Meta's (META) Muse. Microsoft and Nvidia, as well as rivals Apple (AAPL), Intel (INTC), and AMD (AMD), are increasingly pushing the concept of running AI software in the home.
The thinking is pretty straightforward. Rather than having to use an online AI service, you can instead install an app on your computer, download an AI model of your choice, and get to work.
There are some pretty compelling reasons to run AI services on your own machine if you're so inclined. But it's also not for everyone.
When setting up your own AI system makes sense
Running AI locally means you can use AI apps and agents how you see fit without usage limits. You can also choose from a variety of open-weight models from numerous AI developers, such as Google, Meta, and Nvidia, or from Chinese model developers like Moonshot AI and Alibaba Cloud.
Unlike closed-weight models, like OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra or Anthropic's Opus 5.5, open-weight models can be tuned to some extent. But the primary reason users download them is that they're largely free.
Local AI also provides better overall privacy, because your data stays on your machine rather than being sent up to the cloud, an important consideration for people working in fields such as law, medicine, or financial services.
More advanced users have also leaned into running AI on their systems to take advantage of AI agents like OpenClaw that can organize your email, launch and operate apps, and make purchases on your behalf.
The interest in agents sent early adopters scrambling for low-cost computers like Apple's Mac mini, which quickly became hard to come by in AI hotbeds like Silicon Valley.
More recently, AI agents like Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots have introduced similar capabilities via cloud computing. But to take full advantage of those bots, you have to connect things like your Gmail, Uber, and other accounts to them, which means putting a lot of trust in Meta and OpenAI to protect your information.
When to stick to the cloud
While using your computer to run local AI models and agents provides improved privacy and enhanced customization options, doing so is a lot more complicated than simply logging into ChatGPT or Claude.

item.title: Trump disclosed millions in new trades in SpaceX and Microsoft. Today, he gave medals to their CEOs.
item.author: Ben Werschkul
item.description:
Trump disclosed millions in new trades in SpaceX and Microsoft. Today, he gave medals to their CEOs.
2026-10-09
Por Ben Werschkul
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/trump-disclosed-millions-in-new-trades-in-spacex-and-microsoft-today-he-gave-medals-to-their-ceos-182614694.html
Trump disclosed millions in new trades in SpaceX and Microsoft. Today, he gave medals to their CEOs.
President Trump made over 500 securities trades in August in newly disclosed transactions valued at tens of millions of dollars, including in major tech companies whose leaders have become frequent guests at the White House.
According to a new ethics disclosure, Trump made at least 20 trades — a mix of purchases and sales worth millions of dollars — in Nvidia (NVDA), Tesla (TSLA), SpaceX (SPCX), Alphabet (GOOG), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Dell (DELL), and Microsoft (MSFT).
The disclosure was released Thursday, the same day Trump appeared at a "New Golden Age Summit" in Washington, where he presented medals to the heads of those companies.
Trump gave the National Medal of Science to Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Google co-founder Sergey Brin, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and Advanced Micro Devices CEO Lisa Su. Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella received the National Medal of Technology and Innovation.
"We have an extremely high-IQ audience," Trump said at the event as he lavished praise on the leaders and their companies, calling Elon Musk "a national treasure." Trump bought up to $5 million in SpaceX debt in August in the form of senior unsecured notes, the company's inaugural bond issuance, the disclosure shows.
"The entire world is running on Nvidia," Trump said of Jensen Huang and his company.
The new disclosure shows a continued high velocity of trading, particularly in tech stocks, in the president's account.
